countries.name: India
countries.summary: India's higher-education system is overseen by the Ministry of Education and its statutory regulators - the University Grants Commission for universities and degrees, the All India Council for Technical Education for technical and management programmes, and the National Medical Commission for medical education. International applicants normally enter through an institution's own international-admissions office, through the government's Study in India portal, or through a centrally administered scheme such as DASA for engineering and architecture seats at NITs, IIITs and other centrally funded technical institutes. Entry rules differ by nationality, residency status, the prior qualification held and the discipline chosen.
countries.whyStudentsChooseIt: International applicants look at India for English-taught degrees across computing, engineering, management, design, sciences, law and health disciplines, and for a single national application route: the Ministry of Education's Study in India portal issues an SII ID and lets an applicant send one profile to several participating institutes. Government-funded study places also exist through Indian Council for Cultural Relations scholarship schemes, which are applied for through Indian diplomatic missions rather than directly to a university. What an individual applicant can access depends on citizenship, residency status, how the prior qualification is assessed for equivalence, and whether the programme is attached to a national entrance test.
countries.climate: Climate varies widely by region, from alpine Himalayan conditions in the north to tropical coastal and semi-arid zones further south, with a June-to-September monsoon across most of the country.

Graduates work in construction, infrastructure, consultancy and public works, or continue to a master's specialisation.

universities.name: Sardar Raja College of Engineering
universities.summary: Sardar Raja College of Engineering (SRCE) is a private, self-financing engineering college founded in 2000 at Alangulam in Tenkasi district, Tamil Nadu. It is not a university: it is a non-autonomous college affiliated to Anna University, Chennai, which awards its degrees, and its courses are AICTE-approved. It teaches six B.E. branches, a B.Tech in AI and Data Science, and the MCA in English.
universities.campusLifestyle: SRCE's 2026-27 Anna University filing records 16.89 acres at Adaikalapattinam, 40,500 sq m of buildings, a 1,000 sq m library with 40,006 volumes, about 100 networked terminals in the central computing facility, a 5,000 sq m playground, a gymnasium and a 1,000-seat auditorium. The library has subscribed to DELNET since 2003 and carries IEEE journals. Anna University records show about 500 students across all years in 2025-26. The college enforces a dress code and needs 75 per cent attendance to sit university exams.
universities.cityProfile: The campus is at Raja Nagar, Adaikalapattinam, in Alangulam taluk of Tenkasi district, beside the Tenkasi-Tirunelveli highway. The college's Anna University filing describes the site as rural. TNEA's 2026 college guide puts it 19 km from the district headquarters at Tenkasi, with Pavoorchatram the nearest railway station, 10 km away. The college runs its own buses, priced at INR 7,500 to 25,000 a year by route. Older AICTE records still give the district as Tirunelveli, from which Tenkasi district was formed.
universities.practicalExposure: Teaching follows Anna University's curricula and regulations: the university sets the syllabus and conducts end-semester exams, and the college runs internal assessments (three tests per course). AICTE's 2026-27 approval makes an internship mandatory for every admitted student, and Anna University's 2025 regulations give one credit for each two weeks of internship. SRCE's 2026-27 filing lists department laboratories such as Surveying and Levelling, Hydraulic Engineering, Soil Mechanics and Highway Engineering (Civil), Cryptography and Cyber Security (CSE Cyber Security), Electrical Machines I and II and Power laboratories (EEE), and Cloud Computing and Security laboratories (CSE). A training and placement cell is led by a CSE faculty member. In 2026 the college ran a six-day employability course with the Mahindra Pride Classroom of the Naandi Foundation, a GATE awareness session and department visits including an EEE trip to a TNEB substation in Tirunelveli.
universities.hostelOverview: SRCE has its own on-campus hostels: St Joseph Hostel for men and Sophia Raja Ladies Hostel for women, each with 20 three-seat rooms for 60 residents. In 2025-26 they housed 17 men and 6 women. TNEA's 2026 college guide lists room rent at INR 10,000 a year and mess at INR 40,000 a year for both hostels, with no caution deposit or establishment charge. Each hostel has its own kitchen, dining hall and reading room, and the hostel block includes a medical room, a canteen and an indoor games hall.
universities.dietarySupport: The hostel messes serve both vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, according to TNEA's 2026 college guide. The campus has a 300 sq m cafeteria, and drinking water is supplied through coolers on campus. The campus also has a bank extension counter or post facility and a stationery and reprography store. Specific regional or religious diets are not documented, so ask the hostel wardens before joining.
universities.safetyOverview: SRCE has an anti-ragging committee and squad, and its listed anti-ragging phone is 8220077054. The college reports ragging to Anna University and the police. Each hostel has a warden, and the campus has CCTV coverage. Smoking, alcohol and harassment are banned under the college's student rules.
universities.studentSupport: A health centre is staffed by an MBBS doctor, and students are covered by group insurance. A counselling centre gives career guidance, and grievances can be filed through the college's online grievance form. Eligible TNEA entrants can claim the First Graduate concession, the AICTE Tuition Fee Waiver or the Post-Matric Scholarship. Contact: srce@src.org.in or 82200 77052.

faq.question: Is Sardar Raja College of Engineering a university?
faq.answer: No. SRCE is a private, self-financing engineering college run by the Raja Educational and Charitable Trust. It is affiliated to Anna University, Chennai, and is not autonomous, so Anna University sets the curriculum, conducts the end-semester exams and awards the B.E., B.Tech or MCA degree. AICTE approves its courses each year; the 2026-27 approval is dated 13 May 2026.

faq.question: Can international students or NRIs apply to SRCE?
faq.answer: Not on student visas. AICTE's 2026-27 approval for SRCE shows no NRI or international-student seats for any course. TNEA, which fills the government-quota B.E./B.Tech seats, is for Indian nationals. OCI and PIO card holders who are natives of Tamil Nadu may join under open competition, unless they were born abroad after 4 March 2021.

faq.question: Which programmes does SRCE offer in 2026-27?
faq.answer: Anna University affiliation and TNEA 2026 cover seven undergraduate programmes: B.E. Civil, Computer Science and Engineering, CSE (Cyber Security), Electrical and Electronics, Electronics and Communication, and Mechanical Engineering, plus a B.Tech in Artificial Intelligence and Data Science. There is also a two-year MCA. AICTE also lists seven M.E. programmes, but they are not in the college's 2026-27 Anna University filing.

faq.question: How do I get a B.E. or B.Tech seat at SRCE?
faq.answer: Most seats are filled through TNEA, the Tamil Nadu single-window counselling run by DoTE. You register at tneaonline.org, upload your certificates, receive a rank based on Mathematics (100), Physics (50) and Chemistry (50), and choose college code 4968 during counselling. In 2026, registration closed on 5 June and general counselling ran from 20 July to 30 August. Management-quota seats are applied for directly with the college.

faq.question: What marks do I need for B.E./B.Tech admission?
faq.answer: You need a pass in HSC (Class 11 and 12) with Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, averaging at least 45 per cent for the General category or 40 per cent for BC, BCM, MBC/DNC and SC/SCA/ST candidates. A vocational HSC route with an engineering subject is also accepted. There is no entrance exam for TNEA.

faq.question: What does it cost to study at SRCE?
faq.answer: SRCE does not publish its tuition, and TNEA's 2026 guide gives no tuition for the college. Government-quota fees at Tamil Nadu self-financing colleges are fixed by the state fee committee, and management-quota fees are quoted by the college on request. TNEA does list living costs: hostel room INR 10,000 a year, mess INR 40,000 a year and college bus INR 7,500 to 25,000 a year.

faq.question: Are there fee concessions or scholarships?
faq.answer: TNEA entrants can apply for the First Graduate tuition concession, which covers self-financing colleges. The AICTE Tuition Fee Waiver covers up to 5 per cent of B.E./B.Tech seats for families earning under INR 8 lakh a year. SC/SCA/ST candidates with family income under INR 2.5 lakh can get the Post-Matric Scholarship. All are claimed in the TNEA application with e-certificates.

faq.question: How do I join the MCA?
faq.answer: Take TANCET, Anna University's entrance test for MCA and MBA. The 2026 MCA test was on 9 May. You need a three-year bachelor's degree in BCA, B.Sc. IT or Computer Science, or any degree with Mathematics at Class 12 or degree level, with 50 per cent marks (45 per cent for reserved Tamil Nadu categories). SRCE did not offer MCA seats in the 2026 state counselling, so apply to the college directly.

faq.question: When do classes start?
faq.answer: Anna University's calendar for non-autonomous affiliated colleges starts first-semester B.E./B.Tech and MCA classes on 2 September 2026. The last working day of the semester is 17 December, and end-semester exams begin on 22 December 2026. There is one intake a year.

faq.question: What is the teaching language?
faq.answer: English. Anna University's 2025 regulations for affiliated colleges make English the medium of instruction for all B.E./B.Tech, M.E./M.Tech, MCA and MBA programmes. Tamil-medium sections of Civil and Mechanical Engineering exist in the university system but are not listed for SRCE.

faq.question: Is accommodation available?
faq.answer: Yes. SRCE has separate on-campus hostels for men (St Joseph Hostel) and women (Sophia Raja Ladies Hostel), each with 60 places in three-seat rooms. TNEA's 2026 guide lists room rent at INR 10,000 a year and mess at INR 40,000 a year, with vegetarian and non-vegetarian food.

faq.question: Is SRCE accredited by NBA or NAAC?
faq.answer: No. TNEA's 2026 college guide marks every SRCE branch as not NBA-accredited. The college's 2026-27 Anna University filing lists only AICTE approval, with no NAAC grade and no NIRF rank. Its recognition comes from AICTE approval and Anna University affiliation.

faq.question: Is SRCE part of a larger education group?
faq.answer: SRCE was founded by Dr. S.A. Raja and calls itself the third engineering college of the Rajas group. It is run by its own trust, the Raja Educational and Charitable Trust, chaired by Er. A. Jesus Raja. Its degrees are Anna University degrees, not degrees of any group-run private university.

evidence.claimText: The University Grants Commission is the statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education, operating under the Ministry of Education.
evidence.sourceLabel: University Grants Commission (UGC) - official site
evidence.internalNotes: UGC publishes the authoritative lists of Central, State, Deemed-to-be and State Private universities, plus a published list of fake universities. Corroborated by the Study in India portal Indian Higher Education page, which states all institutions are governed by the Ministry of Education.

evidence.claimText: The All India Council for Technical Education is the Government of India statutory body for technical education, covering engineering, management and allied technical programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) - official site

evidence.claimText: The National Medical Commission is the Government of India regulator for medical education and medical institutions; medical and dental admission is governed separately from general higher education.
evidence.sourceLabel: National Medical Commission (NMC) - official site

evidence.claimText: India's higher-education landscape includes over 1,100 universities and more than 45,000 colleges, all governed by the Ministry of Education, and higher education begins after 12 years of schooling.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Indian Higher Education
evidence.internalNotes: Portal-published counts are approximate and shift between AISHE cycles; treat them as indicative and re-check at review. Regulator identity is separately verified against UGC and AICTE.

evidence.claimText: The Study in India portal is the Government of India route for international applicants: the applicant registers for a compulsory SII ID, explores participating institutes and courses, submits applications to several institutes from one profile, accepts an offer letter, then applies for a student visa or student e-visa.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - official portal

evidence.claimText: The Bureau of Immigration directs foreign nationals who wish to apply to Indian institutes to register under the Study in India scheme, confirming the portal as a government-recognised route rather than a third-party service.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: The Indian Council for Cultural Relations administers Government of India scholarship schemes for international students at UG, PG and PhD level, including AYUSH streams; applications are handled through the ICCR A2A scholarship portal and the applicant's Indian diplomatic mission.
evidence.sourceLabel: ICCR Admissions to Alumni (A2A) Scholarship Portal
evidence.internalNotes: Portal states that applicants should contact the Indian Mission for scholarship updates - eligibility and open cycles are mission-specific and vary by country, so no scheme may be presented as open to all nationalities.

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals must obtain a Student Visa to pursue on-campus, full-time structured courses or research at educational institutions recognised by the Government of India. Student (S-3) visas cover yoga, Vedic culture, Indian dance, music and Buddhist studies at approved institutions; Student (S-5) visas cover internships.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India

evidence.claimText: Foreign nationals entering India on a Student visa valid for more than 180 days must register with the jurisdictional FRRO or FRO within 14 days of arrival. Pakistani nationals must register within 24 hours. Children under 12 years and OCI cardholders are exempt from registration, and citizens of Nepal and Bhutan are exempt from both visa and registration requirements.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Registration Requirements
evidence.internalNotes: Corroborated by the Study in India Onboarding & FRRO page, which states e-FRRO registration within 14 days of landing. Nationality-dependent rule - never state one universal deadline.

evidence.claimText: Students on an Indian Student visa must not undertake employment or business activity in India, must open a Non-Resident Ordinary (NRO) account with a recognised Indian bank and furnish the details to the FRRO, and must not enrol in off-campus franchise centres, distance-learning study centres of open universities or outreach programmes.
evidence.sourceLabel: Bureau of Immigration, Ministry of Home Affairs - Study in India
evidence.internalNotes: Directly constrains any work-rights or earn-while-you-study claim on India pages. Do not publish part-time work guidance for India.

evidence.claimText: An applicant should possess proof of admission to a full-time regular academic course at a recognised Indian institution and evidence of financial support, and must also hold a No Objection Certificate from the Ministry of Health where the admission is to a medical or paramedical course.
evidence.sourceLabel: Study in India (Ministry of Education) - Onboarding & FRRO
evidence.internalNotes: The portal adds its own disclaimer that document requirements differ across countries and must be confirmed with the nearest Indian embassy.

evidence.claimText: Admission for Foreign Nationals, OCIs, PIOs and NRIs to undergraduate engineering, architecture and planning programmes at NITs, IIEST, IIITs, SPAs and other centrally funded technical institutes runs through the Ministry of Education DASA scheme, and for the 2026-27 year admission is on the basis of JEE (Main) 2026. DASA seats are supernumerary and capped at up to 15 per cent of a programme's total seats. IITs are outside the DASA scheme.
evidence.sourceLabel: Information Brochure DASA 2026 (UG), Central Seat Allocation Board / Ministry of Education
